summary: Router 0.32.0 (ADR-0096, extends ADR-0095): _Acquire.next_candidate now waits once before any cold pick (a cloud tier, or a local tier whose model is not loaded on the picked node) for a running router-triggered load of the model of a tier ranked before it (new scheduler.tier_loading: claim model equals the tier model or the same blob), at most until the admission deadline, then selects again. For a cloud pick the trigger narrows from any load on a node with a tier's model (loading_for) to a load of the tier's own model. A warm lower tier is still taken at once, so the interactive fallback past a busy loaded model is unchanged. No route, configuration key, destination, payload or CI change.

findings.evidence: Cloud tiers are still reached only through scheduler.choose, which applies Routing.tier_blocked (data class, client floor, provider guards, privacy opt-in) on every selection, including the re-selection after a wait. The change can only replace a cold pick by a higher-ranked tier after its load; it never adds a cloud pick.
findings.resolution: Existing cloud controls apply unchanged; fewer requests reach the cloud or a second local model during loads.

findings.evidence: More requests may wait (cold local picks in addition to cloud picks). The wait reuses _wait_for_load: once per (node, model) via waited_loads, 0.5 s polling, bounded by routing.deadline_ms or max_wait_*, no node slot held. tier_loading only matches unexpired router claims (announce_load, 300 s) for the role's own tier models, so an unrelated load cannot hold requests. A client cannot create claims except by sending ordinary requests that are already admission-limited.
findings.resolution: Bounded as the existing load wait. As before, requests waiting for a load are not counted in admission's max_queue (pre-existing). VRAM use during loads decreases (no second cold model beside a load).

tests.evidence: all PASS (18 checks); with proxy.py from origin/main (0.31.1) the two new waiting checks fail (instrument validated).

tests.command: ruff check .; python test/check_adr_index.py; python test/selftest_control_flow.py; python test/check_control_flow.py
tests.evidence: All checks passed; ADR index ok: 96 ADRs; control flow ok: 0 legacy findings.

limitations: The behaviour during a real model switch is verified after rollout by the staged-question measurement named in ADR-0096, not by this change.
Whether the concurrent second load slowed the first model's load (36 s vs about 15 s) was not isolated.
